title: Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas
description: Purpose, amount and duration of the DIGISOC Scholarship The University of Innsbruck is issuing a Call for Application within the DIGISOC Scholarship Programme, reserved for students enrolled for the Academic Year 2026/2027 in the second year of the Joint Master’s Programme in Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (DIGISOC). The Call for Application has a total budget of EUR 50.000. The DIGISOC Scholarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the DIGISOC Joint Master’s Programme (JMP) and aims to: · Alleviate costs associated with tuition fees, summer schools, short-term mobilities, and living expenses; · Support students from underprivileged or vulnerable backgrounds; · Promote diversity, fairness, and gender balance in higher education. The scholarship also functions as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic obstacles that hinder participation in international education. The DIGISOC Scholarship is limited to one academic year and is paid out in one instalment. There is no automatic entitlement to a scholarship and no automatic renewal. The amount of the scholarship can reach a maximum of EUR 3,000.00 gross per academic year and applicant. The exact amount assigned to each applicant is based on the points awarded in the evaluation process (see Article 5 – Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure). A maximum of 30 points can be awarded to each application. The maximum total funding per student is EUR 6,000.00 over the course of the two-year programme. For the entire academic year for which the scholarship is awarded, the scholarship holder must not have an employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck. Applicants and scholarship holders are solely responsible for clarifying and complying with all tax obligations and any other individual tax consequences arising from receipt of the scholarship. The University of Innsbruck does not provide individual tax advice.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Eligibility Criteria Students enrolled in DIGISOC for the second year are eligible to apply for a scholarship if they meet one or more of the following criteria: 1. Students with certified disabilities Students with certified disabilities can apply for a DIGISOC scholarship. In the context of this call, and following Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, students with disabilities are considered students who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which, in interaction with various barriers, may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of a national disability status. 2. Migrants or refugees Students who are migrants or refugees can apply for funding based on their status. Required proof may include an asylum decision, a residence permit, or confirmation issued by a migration authority. 3. Students with low socio-economic family conditions Students from families with low socio-economic conditions can apply for funding. Low socio-economic conditions are defined according to the student’s family income. Required proof may include a tax statement, an income certificate, or an official social benefit statement. 4. Students living in remote areas Students living in a region in the lowest 25% of national population density and/or with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius may apply. Required proof is a residence certificate, which will be assessed against infrastructure data based on national statistics. Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027 The deadline to submit applications for the DIGISOC scholarships is 10. December 2026 at 23.59 CET (Central European Time). Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link: https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/114518610654144 Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labelled with the applicant’s name: · The signed Application Letter (Annex 1); · The applicant’s registration number (Matrikelnummer) at the University of Innsbruck; · The supporting documentation for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert. · The Data Protection and Consent Declaration (Annex 2). The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; documents in other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application. By submitting the application and signing Annex 1, the applicant expressly confirms that the application has been submitted completely and correctly and that all information and supporting documents are accurate and complete. Incomplete applications may be excluded from the selection procedure. Evaluation Committee A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Study Coordinator (Studienbeauftragter) of the Faculty of Economics and Statistics of the University of Innsbruck, reviews all applications and consists of: · One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree-awarding universities; · At least one student representative from the University of Innsbruck; · Disability officer at the University of Innsbruck. The Committee is appointed after the deadline for application submission and completes the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline. Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure The joint Evaluation Committee will evaluate each application and award points based on the following criteria: 1. Students with certified disabilities Applicants will be awarded points on the basis of the severity and impact of their condition, ranging from 5 points for a comparatively less impactful disability to 10 points for a very serious disability. 2. Migrants or refugees Applicants will be awarded points as follows: a. 10 points for refugee status; b. 10 points for migrant status with less than 5 years in the current country of residence; c. 5 points for migrant status with 5 or more years in the current country of residence. 3. Low socio-economic family condition Applicants will be awarded 10 points if their family income falls within the first quartile (Q1), i.e. within the 25% of the population with the lowest incomes in their country of origin. Applicants will be awarded 5 points if their family income falls between the first and second quartile (Q2), i.e. within the range defined by the median income and Q1 in their country of origin. The reference fiscal year is the year preceding the year in which the application is submitted. 4. Remote areas Applicants will be awarded 5 points for residence in a remote area. An additional 5 points will be awarded if the student’s residence is in a remote area with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius. All applications will be ranked on the basis of the sum of points obtained across the four criteria. Each application can obtain a maximum of 30 points. To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use a proportional point-based model: · Total funds available are divided by the sum of all points awarded across valid applications; · This determines a value per point (EUR/point); · Each applicant receives funding according to their own score, up to the maximum of EUR 3,000.00. The decision of the joint Evaluation Committee is final, subject to the appeal procedure set out in Article 6. The exact amount of funding and its composition awarded to each applicant will be published via the Learning Management System OpenOLAT. This publication constitutes as notification.
furtherInformation:
Acceptance and Appeals

Applicants are notified of decisions within 15 days after the end of the submission period via e-mail. Rejected applications include a short justification.

Applicants who are not awarded a scholarship have the right to appeal. Appeals may be submitted by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at and will be reviewed by the joint Evaluation Committee, including the designated representative responsible for disability, inclusion and/or equal-treatment matters.

Within the mandatory deadline of 5 days from receipt of the scholarship award notice, the applicant must send the declaration of acceptance by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at without reservation and under the conditions of this Call for Application. Failure to do so results in forfeiture of the award.

With the declaration of acceptance, the scholarship holder must also undertake to communicate any change occurring during the academic year that affects information previously declared or eligibility for the scholarship.


Requirements for receiving the scholarship

Before disbursement, the scholarship holder will complete the required scholarship documentation with the University of Innsbruck and must provide:

·       A current enrolment certificate showing the register number;

·       The applicant’s full residential address (street and house number, postal code, city, and country);

·       Bank details for an account held in the scholarship holder’s name, including an IBAN and any further information required to enable a SEPA credit transfer. It must be expressly possible to make the scholarship payment by SEPA transfer to the account provided;

·       A copy of a valid passport or other accepted identification document.

Scholarship holders remain solely responsible for all tax-law clarifications and obligations connected with the scholarship.

The scholarship holder must also confirm that no employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck exists or will exist for the duration of the academic year for which the scholarship is awarded.


Financial and Disbursement Procedures

Scholarships are paid in one instalment per academic year. 

Disbursement is handled by the University of Innsbruck as the DIGISOC degree-awarding university issuing this Call for Application.

Payment will be made by SEPA credit transfer to a current account in the name of the scholarship holder. The account provided must be capable of receiving a SEPA transfer. The scholarship holder is responsible for providing complete and correct bank details and for any bank charges or conversion costs that may arise outside the scope of the SEPA payment.


Renunciation

In the event of withdrawal from the scholarship after acceptance, scholarship holders must give written notice by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at.

In case of transfer to another programme during the 2026/2027 academic year, the scholarship holder will be considered to have renounced the scholarship and must return the full amount of the scholarship.

A scholarship holder who renounces the scholarship is required to return any amounts received, except in duly justified special cases, which will be assessed by the joint Evaluation Committee.


Final provisions

All resources and updates will be made available via the DIGISOC website – Costs and Scholarships page https://digitalsociety4innovation.eu/costs-and-scholarships/

The following templates and tools will be published on the same page:

·       Application and documentation guidelines;

·       Acceptance letter template.

For further questions, please contact:

·       Università degli Studi di Napoli Federico II: digisoc@unina.it

·       Univerzita Palackého v Olomouci, Czechia: digisoc@upol.cz

·       University of Innsbruck, Austria: digisoc@uibk.ac.at


Disclaimer

This Call for Application and the financial support awarded under it do not constitute an EU action. The Call is launched and administered by the University of Innsbruck in its own name and under its own responsibility.

The scholarship programme is partially financed with funds made available to the University of Innsbruck in the framework of the EU-funded EURIDICE / DIGISOC project. Notwithstanding this source of funding, the financial support to successful applicants is awarded and provided directly by the University of Innsbruck. 

The University of Innsbruck remains responsible for the preparation and implementation of this Call, including the application procedure and the selection of successful applicants by the joint Evaluation Committee appointed in accordance with Article 4.

The publication of this Call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information and visibility purposes, including to inform potential applicants. Such publication does not imply any direct or indirect approval, endorsement or validation by the European Union or any of its institutions, bodies or agencies of the content, conditions, selection procedure or outcome of this Call. Nor does such publication transfer to the European Union any responsibility for the administration of the Call or the award of the scholarships, which remains with the University of Innsbruck.

title: Boosting Digital Skills of young pupils, in particular girls
description: The purpose of this call is to identify and support projects that can foster EU Code Week’s mission to promote coding, computational thinking, and digital skills across Europe. The aim is to identify projects that can achieve large-scale impact and deliver on key EU Code Week performance indicators within the project implementation period. Key tasks: Supporting the organisation of a large number of impactful coding, computational thinking, digital skills, and STEM activities; Increasing the number of activities registered on the EU Code Week platform; Reaching a large number of participants through local, regional, national, or cross-border activities; Increasing the participation of girls and young women in coding, digital skills, and STEM education; Supporting career-focused events that introduce students to educational and professional opportunities in STEM and digital fields; Supporting university visits and other activities that strengthen connections between schools, students, and higher-education institutions; Supporting activities and approaches that can be replicated or scaled beyond the project implementation period. Priority will be given to projects that can deliver a large number of activities to the EU Code Week platform and participants while maintaining educational quality and demonstrating clear and measurable impact.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: A selection committee comprising community stakeholders and representatives from the Code4Europe Consortium will evaluate proposals. Each proposal will be assessed based on four main criteria: presentation (clarity and completeness of the application), design congruity (relevance to EU Code Week priorities, coherence and feasibility of activities, and availability of professional and organisational resources), quality (the educational approach, alignment with core digital and literacy competencies, collaboration with local networks, and potential for replicability), and impact (engagement of diverse stakeholders, inclusion of different participant groups, and specific attention to involving girls and fostering STEM education). The evaluation process will be transparent and objective, with measures in place to avoid any conflicts of interest.
furtherInformation:

description: The procedure follows the principles of: transparency, equal treatment, confidentiality, absence of conflict of interest. eligibilityText: The Call has 5 distinct cut-off dates . All submitted applications (for the two objectives/priorities) by each deadline will be evaluated jointly and awarded until funding resources are available. The AI4Gov-X consortium reserves the right of integrating the funding budget with an extra allocation, until twice the initially allocated amount. Applications will be possible electronically and exclusively managed through the GoodGrants TM platform ( https://polidesign.grantplatform.com/ ) by filling in a form and attaching the required documentation. Beneficiaries must be natural persons and as a precondition, be enrolled students in the MagiX master's course (for objectives/priorities 1 and 2) and/or (for objective/priority 1) in one or more of the AI4Gov-X extracurricular activities, strictly identified from the list published on the project's website, at this link: https://ai4gov-x.eu/extracurricular-activities/ . Please note that the list will be updated on a monthly basis while the Call is open. Additionally for objective/priority 2 only, beneficiaries must be unemployed people, able to document the existence of an internship contract with a host organisation from the public or private sector, residing in an eligible country for the Call (for a full list see Further information below). A same natural person holding the necessary requisites may apply to both objectives within the same cut-off date or within two distinct cut-off dates. However, he or she can receive the financial benefits of either objective/priority only once. Evaluation of received applications will be done by a special committee established at the Funding Body, POLI.design . Each application will be evaluated from the perspectives of admissibility, eligibility, and merit. For both priorities/objectives, admissibility conditions will be that an electronic application has been received on or before the latest cut-off date, completed in all its parts, and with all required attachments, exclusively through the GoodGrants TM platform. Incomplete applications or submitted by other means will be discarded and proposed for resubmission at the next cut-off date. To pass the admissibility check, all applicants must submit at least: - A signed application form, - Their CV in Europass format (see https://europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv ), - A motivation letter, specifically mentioning their employment status, - Any documentation supporting disadvantaged background and/or priority categories (where applicable), - Signed declarations (on conflict of interest, double funding, etc.) using the templates available on the GoodGrants TM platform. Applicants to priority/objective 1 must additionally submit: - A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course and/or in an extracurricular activity of the AI4Gov-X programme, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, and - An indicative cost breakdown (travel, accommodation, fees, etc.). Applicants to priority/objective 2 must additionally submit: - A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course, - Copy of an internship contract, or equivalent legally binding agreement, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, showing the amount paid by the host organisation. All the above documentation must be provided in English language . Unofficial translations are allowed in case of submission of documents that are natively not in English, but the applicant will take the risk and bear the consequences of any misinterpretation during the evaluation process. For both priorities/objectives, eligibility conditions will be that - The applicants must be natural persons and nationals of an eligible country for the Call (see Further information below). - They must be enrolled in, or formally accepted into , the MagiX master's course and/or any of the extracurricular activities of AI4Gov-X (depending on the priority/objective) at the time of application. - They must not be subject to restrictive measures or other disqualifying conditions according to the EU or national legislation in their country. - They cannot receive double funding for the same operation. - They cannot be awarded twice under the same priority/objective. - They must not be in a situation of conflict of interest with POLI.design or any other AI4Gov-X partner. For priority/objective 2 only, a supplementary eligibility condition will be that - The applicants must be unemployed people documenting their enrollment in an internship programme at a host organisation residing in an eligible country (see Further information below). Eligible applications received until the same cut-off date will be scored using the following criteria (max. 100 points): Criterion Description Score Excellence and relevance Academic/professional background and relevance to AI4Gov-X topics 0–30 Motivation and expected impact Motivation, expected learning and career impact 0–25 Financial need Economic situation and justification of need 0–25 European added value Cross-border dimension, diversity contribution, EU public sector fit 0–20 No minimum thresholds or weighting will be applied. In case of equal scores, the following priority rules will be adopted, in the same order: - Applicants documenting their enrollment in (or acceptance into) both the MagiX master's course and at least one extracurricular activity of the AI4Gov-X programme (only for objective/priority 1); - Applicants coming from countries that are not full members of the AI4Gov-X consortium. - Applicants from regions with average income below 75% of the EU average. - Female applicants. The maximum financial support per beneficiary is: EUR 5 000 (for both priorities/objectives 1 and 2) The awarded amount for priority/objective 1 is calculated on the basis of: - Actual and justified travel costs, - Actual and justified accommodation costs, - Actual and documented registration/participation fees. as reported in the indicative cost breakdown (see above). The Selection Committee may cap specific cost items if considered excessive or not in line with typical market prices for the location and period. The awarded amount for priority/objective 2 is calculated on the basis of the stipend/salary received by the beneficiary, as documented in the internship contract, or equivalent agreement (see above). For the avoidance of any doubt, the reimbursement of travel and accommodation costs, or other types of cost, is also eligible provided it is explicitly mentioned in the internship contract, or equivalent agreement. For both priorities/objectives, eligible expenses are those realised after the date of submission of the respective application . The priority/objective 1 scheme reimburses up to 50% of total eligible costs, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 156. The priority/objective 2 scheme reimburses an equivalent amount to the one perceived by the intern, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 234.
furtherInformation:
Eligible applicants for both priorities/objectives 1 and 2 must hold the nationality of:

- an EU country;

- the following non-EU countries being eligible to the provisions of the Digital Europe Programme: Albania, Iceland, Kosovo*, Liechtenstein, Montenegro, Norway, North Macedonia, Serbia, Turkey, and Ukraine;

The above list is subject to change in the future without prior advice.

Eligible host organisations for priority/objective 2 must reside in either of the above countries.

title: European Network of Factcheckers
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Fact-checkers are frequently the targets of attacks and harassment as they speak truth to power. The fact-checking community has been repeatedly harassed: individual fact-checkers and organisations have faced threats, vandalised offices, SLAPPs, and coordinated online hate campaigns designed to censor or cancel their work. In response, the consortium comprised of the European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN) , together with its members Faktograf, Pagella Politica, Fact Review, FactCheck Cyprus, and Greece Fact Check , has initiated a protection scheme with the support of the European Union. The primary aim of this scheme is to provide direct, rapid support to fact-checkers in need (e.g. due to online harassment campaigns, hacking attempts, vandalisation of office spaces, threats of physical violence, physical attacks, threats of imprisonment or lawsuits, SLAPPs). Those facing harassment or requiring assistance for their psychological, physical, online or legal safety may submit requests for support under this call. All submissions will be handled with the utmost security and processed as quickly as possible to provide aid to those affected. Support and Eligible Activities Fact-checking organisations can request support for the following: Psychological Support: counselling, burnout prevention, and specialised training. Please note that costs for general staff wellbeing not linked to a specific incident or harassment situation are not eligible. Legal Aid: defence against defamation, harassment, cyber and physical violence, SLAPP suits, copyright disputes, etc. Please note that legal costs related to commercial disputes, employment matters, or issues unrelated to fact-checking activities are not eligible. Safe Workspace: this may include installation of security systems, purchase or rental of security equipment, rental of a secure workspace, or costs to enable staff to work remotely during a period of risk. For fact-checkers, the workspace is understood as the reporting assignment itself and the physical space immediately surrounding it. Emergency Relocation: transport, temporary housing, crisis coordination for teams in danger, etc. Cybersecurity: upgrades for encryption, security tools, and risk assessments, etc. Please note that general IT infrastructure upgrades not linked to a specific security threat or incident are not eligible. Eligibility Criteria To be eligible for funding, applicants must meet the following requirements: Legal entity: applicants must be a legal entity, whether for-profit or non-profit. Certification: applicants must be EFCSN certified fact-checking organisations or fact-checking organisations that can demonstrate they respect in practice the European Code of Standards for Independent Fact-Checking Organisations. Location: organisations must be based in the European Union or DEP-associated countries (see this document for the most up-to-date list). Single applicants: this call is intended for single applicants, i.e. consortia of organisations cannot apply for this call. Budget, Funding, Payment Terms, Grant Duration Total Call Budget: €340,169 Maximum Grant Amount: €20,000 per support request; in exceptional cases (e.g. relocation of a large team), grants can be up to €40,000. Such requests must be reasoned in detail and must be approved by the EFCSN Governance Body in addition to the standard selection procedure outlined below. Funding Rate: 50% Form of Grant: lump sums Number of Grants: ~17 Payment Structure: 75% upon approval of request, 25% following the approval of the final report. Exact amount must be calculated using this template table. List of eligible costs: Direct costs must be directly related to the implementation of the requested support and fall under one of the following categories (although the examples below are not exhaustive): A. Psychological Support: costs related to mental health, wellbeing support, physical checkups related to long-lasting stress, including counselling sessions, burnout prevention activities, and specialised trauma training provided by qualified professionals. B. Legal Aid: costs related to legal support services, including legal counsel or lawyer fees, court or filing fees, legal document translation, notary services, and other directly related legal expenses. C. Physical Safety: costs related to ensuring the physical safety of staff or premises, including security system installation, security equipment purchase or rental, secure workspace rental, remote work setup costs, and related services. D. Emergency Relocation: costs related to urgent relocation and crisis response, including transport, temporary accommodation, crisis coordination services, subsistence costs during relocation, and related support. E. Cybersecurity: costs related to digital security and protection, including security software or tool licences, cybersecurity audits or risk assessments, secure hardware (e.g. encrypted devices), implementation and setup costs, and related services. Retroactive costs: if a grant is approved, costs are eligible from the time of application submission. Indirect / Administrative costs: these are capped at 10% of total direct costs. Max. Grant Duration: 12 months Rolling basis: this call is open on a rolling basis from 2 September 2026 until 31 May 2028 (or until funds are depleted). Selection Procedure The evaluation will be conducted in two steps: Phase 1: AI Processing. The application platform will automatically review submitted applications to ensure that all required information has been provided and that applicants meet the basic eligibility criteria. Phase 2: Expert Evaluation. Requests will be evaluated by the consortium experts based on need, urgency, regional vulnerability, and the applicant’s capacity to absorb the support. Consortium experts may request additional advice from a multidisciplinary group of experts, comprising the Protection Scheme Advisory Board, and escalate particularly delicate decisions to the EFCSN Governance Body. EFCSN will oversee the process, ensuring transparency, financial safeguards, and equitable distribution. Applications will be assessed against the award criteria outlined below. The evaluation is conducted in several steps, depending on the amount and urgency of the request, as shown in the image linked here. The main criteria for evaluating the requests are: Category Description Max. points Need Clear evidence of an acute operational or financial gap directly tied to the emergency situation. Financial statements and other documents may be requested as evidence. 10 Urgency Time-sensitive circumstances where delayed support would meaningfully worsen the outcome. 10 Regional Vulnerability Context of operating environment: political, economic, or press freedom constraints that amplify risk. 10 Absorptive Capacity Organisational ability to receive, manage, and account for the funds in a timely manner. 10 How to Apply and Timeline To apply, please submit your request through the application platform . Requests for urgent support will be processed within 48 hours; other requests will be processed within 5 working days. Reporting An outcome report (financial and narrative) is expected from all grant recipients. Transparency Notice This call has also been published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal. Funding granted through this call will be disclosed on efcsn.com/funding-opportunities . Disclosure will cover the name of the receiving organisation, amount, and grant duration. NB! If a grant recipient operates in a high-risk environment or handles sensitive data, they may request that their identity remains confidential during the implementation phase and be disclosed after the end of the funding cycle. Questions? Please send questions about this call to grants@efcsn.com .

title: I4MS (phase 4) - uptake of digital game changers
description: PULSATE is a part of the Horizon 2020 programme called I4MS funded by the European Commission with the goal to accelerate the design, development and uptake of advanced digital technologies by the European Manufacturing industry to empower personalised products and to facilitate cost-effective small-scale production. One of these digitalization technologies that PULSATE project is focused on is Laser-Based Advanced & Additive Manufacturing (LBAAM). To boost and support the uptake, PULSATE will select and support end-users (Adopters) SMEs and Slightly bigger companies that are willing to implement Laser-Based Advanced & Additive Manufacturing (LBAAM) technologies into their environment. To enable this, PULSATE project brings together a strong consortium comprising six competence centres (AIMEN, FTMC, MTC, SINTEF, Fraunhofer and CEA) with high-level expertise in LBAAM and digitisation, the European Photonics Industry Consortium (EPIC) to support the acceleration of EU innovative scale-up initiatives, and two highly innovative SMEs (CLESGO & Fundingbox) to establish and support the Digital Agora platform, maintain a Marketplace of digital services and to manage the mechanisms of financial support to selected companies and the connection with DIHs across all Europe. Through the 2 nd Open Call for Adopters, PULSATE will select up to 18 Adopter SMEs/Slightly Bigger companies that represent high-potential business use cases for implementation of LBAAM technology in their processes, products and business models. Selected Adopters will take part in a 3-month support programme between january and april 2024, through which they will receive: - Up to €25 000 as a lump sum - Mentorship from PULSATE Consortium partners in LBAAM feasibility assessment that will allow Adopters to confirm Technical and Business Feasibility for the implementation of LBBAM technology in their environment.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Applications must be submitted via https://pulsate-adopters.fundingbox.com . The selection of the open call proposals will be carried out in a four-step process: Step 1 will check the proposals against eligibility criteria. Step 2 will involve external evaluation to assess the proposal according to the criteria. Step 3 will involve the PULSATE consortium to prioritise the proposals based on the external evaluation results and the objectives of the PULSATE project. Step 4 legal check before finalists are invited to sign the Sub Grant Agreement. For further information see the Guide for Applicants section 4. Applicants eligibility PULSATE is looking for End-user / Technology Adopter companies that are interested in the implementation of LBAAM technology into their environment that will enhance the activities of the manufacturing industry. Adopters should represent high-potential business Use Cases for implementation of Laser-Based Advanced and Additive Manufacturing (LBAAM) technology in their processes, products and business models. Applications can be submitted by only ONE company that has the status of SMEs or a Slightly Bigger company and is legally established in one of the eligible countries. For further information see the Guide for Applicants section 3.
furtherInformation:
• Main Open Call and application website where all documents can be found: https://pulsate-adopters.fundingbox.com
  • Helpdesk email: pulsate.help@fundingbox.com
  • PULSATE website for general information about the project: https://www.pulsate.eu
  • PULSATE community (https://spaces.fundingbox.com/spaces/i4ms-pulsate-open-calls-helpdesk)
